title: Path traversal out of the web root
root_cause: A user-supplied name is joined onto a base directory and handed to the filesystem, which happily resolves '..' segments, symlinks and absolute paths. The program checked (or assumed) the name was a file inside the folder, but the operating system interprets it as a path.
defenses: Canonicalize first (resolve + realpath), then check the result is inside the allowed directory -- never check the raw string.
Prefer an allow-list or an ID lookup (files/<id>) over accepting file names from users at all.
Reject absolute paths, NUL bytes and path separators in names that should be a single file name.
Run the service with a filesystem view limited to the data it needs (chroot, container mounts, read-only roots).
Remember symlinks: a lexical prefix check alone is not enough.
